To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) habitat fragmentation increases disease outbreaks and intensification of disease persistence; (2) the risk of infection is reduced when the distribution of the vectors is proportional to that the hosts; and (3) human movement and mosquito movement can both decrease the infection risk, and the total number of the infected humans can also be decreased by mosquito movement, but not by human movement.
